_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::structural_dynamics#5, and a FALSIFICATION of it. The entry said ConstDisVelAcc is the recommended (and implicitly default) predictor and that TangDis costs more Newton iterations. On a transient inline HEX8 cantilever under GenAlpha, 4C echoes '=== Structural predictor: ConstDis ===' when PREDICT is not set, so the default is ConstDis; setting PREDICT: ConstDis reproduces the default exactly (24 total Newton iterations over 8 steps, same as the default arm); ConstDisVelAcc costs 31 and TangDis costs 16, i.e. TangDis is the CHEAPEST of the three here, the opposite of the claim. All arms exit 0. A near-miss spelling ('ConstDisVelAccel') is rejected at parse with 'Could not match this input', so the choice cannot go wrong silently. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the discriminating arm: make the TangDis deck use ConstDisVelAcc instead. ITERS_TANGDIS then equals the ConstDisVelAcc count and the numeric contrast that carries the correction disappears, so the fixture must go red.
remove the second pathology: spell the enum correctly in the typo arm. The parse error vanishes and EXIT_TYPO becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
